title: TrustMI: Causally controlling how assistants trust their users
abstract: arXiv:2610.06064v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) assistants routinely decide whether they can trust users and third parties whose competence, intentions, and integrity they cannot verify. This uncertainty matters for safety, as trusting the wrong party can lead an agent to comply with harmful requests or act on malicious instructions encountered during tool use. To study this problem, we define trust as an assistant's willingness to accept vulnerability to the actions of another party and ask whether such behavior can be causally controlled through model activations. We build 2,000 contrastive conversations spanning ability, benevolence, and integrity, where paired responses complete the same request but differ in whether the assistant trusts the user. From these pairs, we learn steering matrices while keeping the model parameters frozen and test them across six instruction-tuned models from three families, finding that steering changes trust decisions mo

translated_title: TrustMI：因果性地控制助手如何信任其用户
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）助手经常需要决定是否信任那些其能力、意图和诚信均无法验证的用户与第三方。这种不确定性对安全至关重要，因为信任错误的方可能导致智能体服从有害请求，或在工具使用过程中依据遭遇的恶意指令采取行动。为了研究这一问题，我们将信任定义为助手愿意接受另一方行为所带来的脆弱性，并探究这种行为能否通过模型激活进行因果控制。我们构建了2000段涵盖能力、善意与诚信三个维度的对比对话，其中配对的回复完成相同的请求，但在助手是否信任用户这一点上存在差异。基于这些对话对，我们在保持模型参数冻结的条件下学习转向矩阵，并在来自三个模型家族的六个指令微调模型上进行测试，发现转向能够改变信任决策……
tldr: 该论文提出TrustMI，通过构建2000段涵盖能力、善意与诚信的对比对话并学习激活转向矩阵，在冻结模型参数的情况下因果性地控制LLM助手对用户的信任决策，从而提升智能体安全性。
en_tdlr: TrustMI causally controls how LLM assistants trust their users by learning activation steering matrices from 2,000 contrastive conversations spanning ability, benevolence, and integrity—while keeping model parameters frozen—thereby improving agent safety.
